source: retroactive audit at adoption; see lupine-science PR #51
trackedBy: Hermes t_1f48ad62 (narration shortfall) and t_22034221 (audio gate)
policy: Known failing checks per film are reported, not blocking. Any NEW failing check, or any film not listed, fails the gate closed. Remove entries as films are fixed; never add entries to make CI pass.

revisions.change: Half-speed repair: the 10 article films were re-rendered from their original un-stretched narration wavs, undoing the published `atempo=0.5` artifact. Measured speech rate doubled on every one of the 10 (21-66 wpm -> 43-131 wpm) and every film's duration halved with audio/video still matched. Removed 5 entries: a-field-not-a-neural-net and five-materials-for-5-to-12-gtco2-year now pass every check and are delisted; the-02-percent-synthesis-problem lost no-dead-air-during-narration. Films: 29 -> 27.
revisions.whySpeechRateEntriesRemain: The 8 article films still listed for speech-rate-in-band are NO LONGER half-speed. Their published .vtt is the scene-title placeholder written by scripts/generate-motion-vtt.mjs, which that script itself flags as needing alignment to the actual narration. It carries only 35-74 words across the whole film, so the gate divides real narration time by placeholder word counts and reports 43-98 wpm. Measured against the audio itself (faster-whisper small.en and medium.en) the repaired narration runs 118-144 wpm on all 10 films - inside the band. Clearing these entries requires narration-transcript captions, which requires re-narration: the cached Orpheus wavs deliver only 30-45% of the intended script and contain hallucinated passages, so transcribing them would publish gibberish into a <track ... default> caption that the site shows by default. Do not remove these entries by swapping in transcripts of the corrupted audio.

revisions.change: Narration rebuild: all 10 article films were re-narrated from the intended scripts (recovered from the pre-overwrite VTTs at commit 4641d96 into data/narration-scripts/) using MiniMax speech-2.8-hd instead of the locked FAL Orpheus account, and each .vtt was regenerated from the verified narration itself. Every track is now length-verified against its word count before it is accepted: the films deliver 104-117% of expected length at 124-140 wpm, against 29-67% before. Normalization is two-pass (linear) and the narration stays PCM until the muxer's single AAC encode, which is what makes true-peak reproducible. Removed 13 entries across 10 films, all of which now pass every check: films 29 -> 19.
revisions.whySpeechRateEntriesAreGone: The published .vtt for these films is no longer the scene-title placeholder written by scripts/generate-motion-vtt.mjs. Each cue is now one sentence of the actual script, synthesized as its own audio file and timed by that file's measured duration, so speech-rate-in-band divides real narration time by the real spoken word count instead of by 35-74 placeholder words. The check measures what it was built to measure, and passes on its own terms.
revisions.supersedes: PR #59 (merged as be16b24) repaired the half-speed artifact by re-rendering these same ten films from their cached Orpheus narration. That narration was itself content-corrupted (29-67% of the intended script), which #59 documented and deliberately left in place. These ten films are now re-narrated from the recovered scripts, so #59's renders are superseded for them; its entry above is kept because it is the record of how the speech-rate numbers moved first.
